headline: Volume is building steadily and easy-run cardiac drift is tracking downward — aerobic efficiency is moving in the right direction.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your recent four-week block represents a meaningful step up in load, and the pace of that increase sits well within sustainable progression territory. More telling than the volume number itself is what's happening at easy effort: heart rate on comparable runs has dropped noticeably relative to the prior block, which points to genuine aerobic adaptation rather than just accumulated mileage. That's the kind of signal worth tracking.

The 20-week running streak — now matching your personal best — is background context worth acknowledging without over-reading. Streaks carry compounding load that isn't always visible in weekly numbers, and with strength consistency holding firm across both blocks, total systemic demand is real. Nothing here flags concern, but it's worth staying honest about cumulative fatigue as the streak extends beyond familiar territory.

The lactate threshold data point from 2026-07-02 is recent and isolated — a single test is insufficient to trend, but a threshold at that pace and heart rate is consistent with the fitness picture the volume and HR data are already sketching.
watch_items: Watch whether easy-run HR continues to trend downward or plateaus — this is the clearest live signal of aerobic adaptation right now.
Monitor how the body responds to continued streak extension beyond 20 weeks — this is uncharted personal territory and internal fatigue cues become more important.
As the lactate threshold baseline accumulates more data points, watch whether subsequent tests confirm or challenge this first reading.
Note whether strength session quality holds as running volume continues to build — degradation there would be the first sign of total-load saturation.
